SBP: Did the resident seek information to determine if the patient had assigned a health-care proxy and/or previously discussed preferences regarding end-of-life issues with family members?
Did the resident summarize the agreed-upon short-term and long-term goals, identifying additional resources (clergy, ethicist, etc…) and asking if there are further questions or comments?
ICS: Did the resident introduce himself or herself, and introduce and delineate the roles of each of the persons present at the meeting?
Did the resident begin the conversation with open-ended questions to assess the family’s level of understanding the situation?
Did resident positively focus the conversation (i.e., everyone is here to try to do what is best for the patient)?
Did the resident communicate the patient’s condition using language the family members could understand?

Did the resident communicate the severity of illness including: i. Clearly conveying the number of organ systems involved? ii. Qualitatively describing the overall likelihood of survival without using percentages?
Did s/he use clear, straightforward language such as “he is likely to die?”

Did resident explore short-term and long-term goals with the family, explicitly describing what they believe the most likely short-term and long-term outcomes would be and whether these are achievable?
